name: Oromo
notes:
Oromo (Afaan Oromoo) in Qubee Latin orthography, official in Ethiopia since 1991. Vowel length is phonemic and written with doubled letters; the short vowels are also laxer and more centralised than their long counterparts, so are /ɐ ɛ ɪ ɔ ʊ/ against long /ɑː eː iː oː uː/ (Abu et al. 2025, Table I). Consonant gemination is likewise phonemic and written with doubled letters, which the doubled graphemes reproduce directly. Table II of Abu et al. 2025 gives the Qubee letters and their glottalised-stop / implosive classes after Griefenow-Mewis 2001, with the IPA values following from the places of articulation it assigns: the glottalised stop series is written = /pʼ tʼ tʃʼ kʼ/, and is the implosive of that class, /ᶑ/; <'> is the glottal stop /ʔ/. The Wikipedia Oromo-phonology summary and Owens 1985, describing Harar Oromo, call the implosive retroflex rather than alveolar/dental; that place value is followed here since Table II itself only marks the class, not the exact place. Owens 1985 also describes as uvular for Harar Oromo; the velar value given here follows the written-Oromo standard.

and occur only in loanwords and proper names and are given their plain IPA values /p v/; Table II marks the whole set (p) (v) (z) as loanword-only segments outside the native consonant inventory. Qubee does not write the pitch accent, so no tone is emitted.
